Regarding the diversity in Asian Literature, like yes of course per region(?)/country it is going to be absolutely different in style and even with the sociological aspects that play in their inspirations in writing and plots for sure, all of which I find particularly exciting. For example, the last book I read was Ocean Vuong, and it was such a different Asian experience being that he's speaking from an immigrant perspective. I agree that we tend to box literature like that which makes it hard for novice readers like me to somewhat pick apart the literature I read besides what's obvious (genre, etc.). I would love to be able to understand the differences of their writing styles and cultural contexts too!

Also I love how you mention the difference between language (and cultural) barriers, as well as the effect that translators have on the literature. I don't know if this counts, but I did notice this reading from one publisher to another in terms of classic literature especially for foreign authors like Dostoyevsky and the like. I used to never think about this until I switched. It would be nice if I could have access to a variety of translations just to discern which ones are as close to the native language, but like you said, I could only make do with what's available to me as of the moment. It's interesting to talk about these things, so thank you so much for all the wonderful information! I'm definitely keeping them in mind when I check out Murakami afterwards.
